clue.text: Iron ration ? Nonsense !

definitions.meaning: jokingly, the ration an iron of the grid-patterned breakfast kind turns out: a batter cake

explanation.surface: A soldier dismisses his emergency iron ration as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: An iron ration is a soldier's emergency pack; here the iron is the kitchen appliance that bakes batter in a grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A waffle iron bakes batter cakes, and to talk at length saying nothing is the same word for empty verbiage.

clue.text: A cereal fruit in its cup

parts.note: corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A grain fruit served in its bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: The oak's nut sits in a small cup-shaped base, the cupule.

clue.text: Time of year to figure out a cooling drink

parts.note: Feb is short for February, a month

indicators.note: out signals the letters of figure are scrambled

explanation.surface: A month in which to work out a refreshing beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure out' looks like 'solve'; here 'out' is the anagram signal, and a febrifuge is strictly a fever-reducing medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A febrifuge is a medicine that reduces fever, so a draught that cools the patient.

clue.text: Test driver drops a letter, gets a packet

definitions.note: the clue gives a verb phrase describing what this noun does

indicators.note: L is the letter, the L-plate shown by a learner, which is dropped

parts.note: a learner driver takes the driving test

explanation.surface: A learner driver loses his L-plate and earns a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: A British learner driver displays an L-plate, so the letter dropped is L. To 'make a packet' is British slang for earning a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: An earner is someone who makes money, here one who makes a packet, a large sum.

clue.text: School half, not one though for Gilbert's maids

parts.note: semi- is the prefix meaning half
nary is dialect for not a single one

explanation.surface: A remark on a part-time school that Gilbert's maids never attended.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Mikado, Gilbert's three little maids 'come from a ladies' seminary', so 'though for Gilbert's maids' is a nod confirming the school.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminary is an academy or college, in older use a boarding establishment for young ladies.

clue.text: Its passenger is over the hump, sighting dry land

definitions.text: Its passenger is over the hump, sighting dry land

parts.words: Its passenger is over the hump, sighting dry land
parts.note: a rider sits atop a humped beast crossing arid sand, likened to a vessel at sea

explanation.surface: A traveller over the worst, finally seeing land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the hump' means past the worst, but the rider literally sits above the camel's hump; 'dry land' is the arid sand it crosses.
explanation.definitionFit: The camel is nicknamed for carrying travellers across the sands like a vessel crossing the ocean.

clue.text: Little monkey wreaks some havoc in a trade centre

indicators.note: in places the scrambled letters inside the trade centre

parts.note: a mart is a market, a centre of trade

indicators.note: wreaking havoc on a word throws its letters about
havoc completes the phrase that jumbles the word some

explanation.surface: A small monkey causes chaos in a market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wreaks some havoc' reads as a phrase about mischief, but 'wreaks ... havoc' is the anagram signal working on 'some' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmosets are tiny South American monkeys.

clue.text: Unfriendly cactus ?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, saying one is not a friend
a prickly pear cactus of Mexico

explanation.surface: A prickly cactus is not a welcoming plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the word says 'not a mate', and whole it names the prickly pear of Mexico.

clue.text: Like this rogue, converted

indicators.note: converted letters are changed into a new form, so this and rogue are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reformed villain becomes virtuous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges THIS ROGUE; the whole clue describes a reformed rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A converted sinner becomes morally upright and virtuous.

clue.text: Nco takes on the robber maid disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed letters are thrown out of order, so the words robber and maid are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sergeant-type soldier tackles a thief and a flustered maid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' shuffles ROBBER MAID; 'takes on the' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombardier is a non-commissioned rank in the British artillery, equivalent to corporal.

clue.text: Unlikely fliers embayed in Cuba

definitions.meaning: from the saying that something will happen when these farm animals fly
the Bay of the same name in Cuba, site of the failed 1961 invasion

explanation.surface: Improbable airmen trapped in a Cuban bay.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmyard swine are proverbially unable to fly, and the Cuban inlet of the 1961 invasion is the Bay of the same swine.

clue.text: Novel idol with feet of clay

definitions.text: Novel idol with feet of clay

parts.words: Novel idol with feet of clay
parts.note: the central figure of a novel who is flawed rather than admirable, a hero with weaknesses

explanation.surface: A newly worshipped idol turns out to have flaws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like 'new' but means a work of fiction, whose flawed protagonist is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A protagonist lacking conventional heroic virtues is a flawed central character, a hero with feet of clay.

clue.text: One dedicated to the Round Table movement

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: movement of the letters of table means they are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A knight devoted to King Arthur's Round Table fellowship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round Table' reads as Arthurian, but the two words split: 'Round' is a shape and 'movement' acts on 'Table'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblate is a layperson offered or devoted to religious life, often in a monastery.

clue.text: Cabbage as a teatime delicacy ?

definitions.meaning: the French word for this vegetable
a little pastry puff, as in choux pastry

explanation.surface: Is cabbage really something to serve at tea?
explanation.definitionFit: The French for cabbage also names a small cream puff of choux pastry served as a teatime treat.

clue.text: Extra lift: a highball gives the section

parts.note: hyper- is a prefix meaning extra or beyond

indicators.note: in a down clue, lift raises the letters so they read bottom to top

parts.note: a lob is a high ball in tennis or cricket

explanation.surface: An extra boost: a whisky highball does the trick.
explanation.walkthrough: A highball is a whisky drink, but here it is a high ball in sport; 'lift' turns the pieces upward in a down clue, and 'the section' is a conic section.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyperbola is one of the conic sections, the curve cut from a cone by a steep plane.

clue.text: Jumper of the clinging kind with trunks

definitions.text: Jumper of the clinging kind with trunks

parts.words: Jumper of the clinging kind with trunks
parts.note: an amphibian that leaps and clings to the trunks of forest growth

explanation.surface: A clingy sweater worn with swimming trunks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' and 'trunks' suggest clothing (a jumper is a British sweater), but the jumper is an amphibian and the trunks are timber.
explanation.definitionFit: This amphibian has sticky toe pads for clinging to bark as it leaps among branches.

clue.text: He's not at home

parts.note: read as someone not in his native country rather than out of the house

explanation.surface: A caller is told the man of the house is out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not at home' suggests out of the house, but means not in one's own country.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from another country is away from his homeland, an alien.

clue.text: Perennial wish Methuselah complied with

definitions.meaning: lasting the whole length of time, as in the whole day
Methuselah lived 969 years, fulfilling the wish to survive for ages

explanation.surface: Methuselah obeyed an everlasting wish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting a full span means perennial, and Methuselah obeyed the wish to survive many years.

clue.text: The desire of a quiet little French girl

parts.note: p is the musical marking piano, quiet
petite is French for little, in the feminine form

explanation.surface: Longing for a demure, small French girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetite is a craving or wish for something, especially food.

clue.text: A get-up favoured by the 4

definitions.meaning: the act of getting up from bed
4 down is the earner, who welcomes an increase in pay

explanation.surface: An outfit popular with a wage-earner.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' points to 4 down, EARNER; a wage-earner welcomes a pay increase. 'get-up' looks like an outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting out of bed is rising, and an increase in wages is likewise this word, welcomed by anyone earning.

clue.text: A lot there when the king is welcomed on arrival

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
to meet someone is to greet them when they arrive

explanation.surface: Plenty of people turn out to greet the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot' looks like 'many' but means one's lot in life, destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is fate or destiny, one's allotted portion in life.

clue.text: Nothing clear anyway in its pronouncements

definitions.text: Nothing clear anyway in its pronouncements

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: anyway means in any order at all, so the letters of clear are jumbled

explanation.surface: A seer's sayings are never clear whichever way you read them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' is the anagram signal; the whole clue also describes the famously ambiguous sayings of Delphi.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle was a shrine or prophet whose cryptic replies were notoriously ambiguous.

clue.text: Course held by an American alighting on Mars ?

indicators.note: held by means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A route followed by an American astronaut landing on Mars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' finds the word in americAN ALighting; 'on Mars ?' recalls the canals once thought to cross the Martian surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is an artificial watercourse, and old astronomers claimed to see such channels on Mars.

clue.text: Fit to be Mrs Bennet's son-in-law

definitions.meaning: Mrs Bennet in Pride and Prejudice hunts for single men worth marrying to her daughters

explanation.surface: Suitable to marry one of Mrs Bennet's daughters.
explanation.definitionFit: Qualified means suitable, and Austen's Mrs Bennet seeks marriageable bachelors of good fortune for her girls.

clue.text: Rights to stories about Nationalist leader

indicators.note: about means the fibs go around the next letter

parts.note: stories in the sense of untruths, fibs

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Claims to tales about a nationalist chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stories' suggests tales but means fibs; 'about' wraps them round the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Liens are legal claims or entitlements to hold property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: Continue with the dope

definitions.meaning: to carry on, as a two-word phrase
a dope is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: Keep going with the drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on is a two-word phrasal verb meaning proceed, and a stupid person is a dolt or nitwit.

clue.text: Mural ornament the boss allowed to be put back

parts.note: an overman is a foreman or supervisor

indicators.note: put back means turned round, so the word for allowed is read backwards

parts.note: let means allowed

explanation.surface: A decoration the manager permitted to be replaced on the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: An overmantel is an ornamental shelf or mirror frame fixed on the wall above a fireplace.

clue.text: March, advance warning given, saved by the clock

definitions.text: March, advance warning given, saved by the clock

parts.words: March, advance warning given, saved by the clock
parts.note: in spring the clocks go forward an hour to save evening light

explanation.surface: A protest march, warned of in advance, stopped in time by the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' reads as a protest; it is the month when British clocks advance an hour for summer time, so evening light is saved.
explanation.definitionFit: Clocks advance in March to save the light of day in the evenings, as daylight saving time.

clue.text: Horses don't like this bird getting under their feet

definitions.meaning: an infection of the frog of a horse's hoof
a songbird such as the song or mistle kind

explanation.surface: Horses dislike a bird that gets under their hooves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting under their feet' places the horse's complaint in the hoof, where this infection rots the frog.
explanation.definitionFit: A songbird of the genus Turdus shares its name with a hoof infection afflicting horses.
